Formal Verification Pipeline Architecture

The BNS Legal Reasoning Verification System replaces stochastic black-box LLM predictions with deterministic, auditable, and mathematically sound First-Order Logic deduction.

Stage 1
Statutory Ingestion
Official Gazette text of Act No. 45 of 2023 parsed into 1,301 atomic components and 1,355 statutory relationships.
Stage 2
FOL Translation
1:1 Syntactic isomorphism maps each statutory clause to a formal Horn clause or non-monotonic defeasible override rule.
Stage 3
Fact Assertion
Factual scenario represented in Kleene 3-valued logic: True, False, or Unknown (Open-World Assumption).
Stage 4
Deduction Engine
Forward-chaining inference tests prima facie offence rules and resolves exception overrides without closed-world leaps.
Stage 5
Audit Trail & Verdict
Produces provable verdict (Proved, Refuted, Open) with complete statutory citations and execution traces.

Open-World Assumption vs Closed-World

Standard LLMs and Prolog engines adopt the Closed-World Assumption (Negation as Failure), treating unstated facts as false. In criminal jurisprudence, this causes disastrous hallucinations (convicting without proving mens rea).

Kleene 3-Valued Logic:
• True (1): Explicitly proved by evidence
• False (0): Explicitly disproved by evidence
• Unknown (⊥): Unproven / missing evidence

Defeasible Non-Monotonic Override

Exceptions in criminal codes (e.g. Sec 101 Exceptions 1-5, General Exceptions Sec 14-44) operate non-monotonically: proving an affirmative defence overrides a prima facie offence.

Formal Scheme:
1. Offence: PrimaFacieMurder(x,y) ∧ ¬ExceptedFromMurder(x,y) → Murder(x,y)
2. Override: Exception1(x,y) → ExceptedFromMurder(x,y)
3. Mitigation: PrimaFacieMurder(x,y) ∧ ExceptedFromMurder(x,y) → MitigatedOffence(x,y)
